ordered_diagnoses: Extranodal natural killer/T-cell lymphoma, nasal type

s1.syndrome_frame: febrile illness with rash and hypotension in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: erythematous patches and thin plaques with telangiectases and hyperpigmentation
intravascular atypical cells on skin biopsy
key_facts: patient is a woman in her 50s
history of chronic pulmonary coccidiomycosis
being treated with fluconazole
admitted for fever, hypotension, and rash
previous reaction to pembrolizumab
new skin eruption is widespread and asymptomatic
skin eruption has been ongoing for 1 to 2 weeks
white blood cell count is 4100/μL
absolute neutrophil count is 2940/μL
hemoglobin level is 8.2 g/dL
platelet count is 62 ×10^3/μL
blood culture results show no growth at 1 week
serum β-D-glucan, galactomannan, Coccidioides antibody, and immunodiffusion results are negative
respiratory viral panel and SARS-CoV-2 test results are negative

shortlist.label: Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: skin biopsy findings showing intravascular atypical cells

shortlist.label: Intravascular natural killer/T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: skin biopsy findings and immunocompromised state

shortlist.label: Extranodal natural killer/T-cell lymphoma, nasal type
Pembrolizumab-associated cutaneous adverse reaction
shortlist.why_kept: history of pembrolizumab treatment and new skin eruption

raw.rationale: The presence of intravascular atypical cells on skin biopsy, particularly with CD56 immunostaining, along with the patient's symptoms of fever, hypotension, and rash, and the absence of infection evidence, points towards a lymphoma. The patient's previous reaction to pembrolizumab and the new skin eruption could be related but the biopsy findings specifically suggest a lymphomatous process.

rejected.label: Intravascular natural killer/T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: While CD56 immunostaining is positive, which can be seen in natural killer/T-cell lymphomas, the clinical presentation and other biopsy findings are more indicative of a B-cell lymphoma.

rejected.label: Extranodal natural killer/T-cell lymphoma, nasal type
rejected.why: The clinical presentation does not specifically suggest involvement of the nasal area or other extranodal sites typical for this lymphoma.

rejected.label: Angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with systemic symptoms, lymphadenopathy, and specific laboratory findings such as elevated liver enzymes and polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia, which are not highlighted in the case.

rejected.label: Pembrolizumab-associated cutaneous adverse reaction
rejected.why: While the patient had a previous reaction to pembrolizumab, the new skin eruption and biopsy findings suggest a more serious underlying condition, specifically a lymphoma, rather than a simple adverse reaction to the drug.
